A.notes: A has a strong hero and a coherent earthy editorial mood; the large serif and simplified cup illustration make the featured product feel distinctive and shoppable. The firing story is conceptually on-brief, but the motion evidence is modest and on mobile the process graphic appears to collapse or disappear, which hurts craft. Accessibility is not gate-safe because of measured contrast failures, though keyboard reach and reduced-motion support are present.

B.notes: B is more structured and more obviously e-commerce, with a refined editorial system of tables, rules and product rows that keeps buying fast. The scroll-frame strip shows the clearest motion concept: the cup and step sequence progress from stack to fire to cool in a way that directly serves the brief; I cannot judge easing from stills. It is held back by more contrast failures and font-loading errors, but visually it is the more complete and controlled design.

raw.why: B better integrates shopping and story, and its scroll sequence is the only one that clearly uses motion to narrate the firing process.
